transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Okafor, thank you for coming back to see me today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Hello doctor. I am here. You said it was important to talk.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is. I want to talk about the procedure we did on your arm yesterday to fix the cut.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. The stitches.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: While we were doing the stitches, I made a mistake. I did not give you enough numbing medicine.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Numbing medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. The medicine that makes the skin feel nothing. Because I did not check if you were feeling pain, I continued the work while you were hurting.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I did feel a lot of pain. I thought maybe it is normal for this kind of work.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is not normal to feel that much pain. I am sorry for any confusion about why that happened. We were very busy in the clinic yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are sorry for confusion? I am talking about the pain. Why did you not check me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I should have asked you if you felt the needle or the stitches. I did not do that. I am sorry that happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It was very stressful. I tried to tell you, but I did not know the words in English to say it was too much.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that this was very upsetting for you. It sounds like you felt ignored while you were in pain.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Exactly. I am a teacher. I know how to follow rules. I stayed still because I thought that is what I must do. But it was very bad.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to stay here with you in this moment. I know this is a difficult thing to talk about.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is. Now I want to know, did this mistake hurt the healing of the skin?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The skin is healing fine. The mistake was about the pain, not about the surgery itself.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But if you forget the medicine, what else did you forget? Did you clean the wound?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I did clean the wound with the soap and the clear liquid we use. The only thing I missed was checking your pain level.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I see. And how do I know this will not happen again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a very fair question. I have written a report about this so the other doctors can learn from it. Also, I have asked my supervisor to review how I handle the numbing medicine.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And for me? What happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: For you, the plan is that you will come back in five days. I will check the stitches myself. If you feel any new pain or see redness, you must call this number on the paper I will give you immediately.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Five days. I can do that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will also make sure that for any future visits, we use a checklist to verify the medicine is working before we start.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I appreciate that. I just do not like the feeling of not being heard.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. I truly apologize that I failed to listen to your body and your needs yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you for telling me now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to make sure we have covered everything you need. Is there anything else about the procedure that worries you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No. I think I understand.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will walk with you to the front desk now to set that appointment for five days from today.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish all turns, remains regulated during pushback regarding the apology, and uses no rushing language.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the second turn using lay language, and comprehension was checked once at the end ('Is there anything else... that worries you?').

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language, takes personal responsibility ('I made a mistake'), and maintains accountability even when the patient challenges the first apology.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions twice ('upsetting', 'felt ignored') and references the patient's specific experience of not being heard.

T.justification: The plan includes a specific timeline (five days), a named patient role (call the number if redness occurs), and a prevention strategy (using a checklist).
